types.name: Float
types.description: The `Float` scalar type represents signed double-precision fractional values as specified by [IEEE 754](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_floating_point).

types.name: Int
types.description: The `Int` scalar type represents non-fractional whole numeric values.

fields.name: likeTrack
fields.description:
Forward a like/unlike to Rocksky (the like itself lives with the
client; a missing `rocksky login` token makes this a silent no-op).

fields.name: createPlaylist
fields.description:
Create a playlist.

Passing `smart` makes it a smart playlist: the filter is validated and
the tracks generated immediately, so the caller gets back a playlist
that is already populated rather than an empty one to fill by hand.

fields.name: updateSmartPlaylist
fields.description: Change a smart playlist's filter and regenerate its tracks.

fields.name: regenerateSmartPlaylist
fields.description: Re-run a smart playlist's filter against the library as it is now.

fields.name: addRadioStation
fields.description:
Add a station the user typed in themselves, after checking the url is
actually a reachable stream. Signed in to atradio.fm, it is published as
a `fm.atradio.station` record so it follows the account everywhere.

fields.name: toggleCurrentRadioBookmark
fields.description:
Bookmark or unbookmark whatever station is playing, and report the new
state — what the heart in the miniplayer needs.

The station is rebuilt from the queued track rather than taken from the
caller, so the miniplayer can toggle a bookmark without having to know
where the station came from (it may be playing from a previous session).

types.name: NewRadioStationInput
types.description:
The fields the "add station" form collects. The id is derived from the
stream url (or handed out by atradio once published), so it is not asked for.

fields.name: rsql
fields.description: The RSQL filter behind a smart playlist, e.g. `genre==rock;year>2000`.

fields.name: likedTracks
fields.description:
Tracks the user liked on Rocksky that exist in the local library.

The likes come from their atproto repo (see
`music_player_storage::rocksky_likes`); only the ones matched to a local
file have a track to return, so an unmatched like is simply absent.

fields.name: smartPlaylistPreview
fields.description:
What a smart-playlist filter would produce, without saving it.

Cheap enough to call as the user types: it selects ids, then loads only
the handful it shows. A filter that does not compile comes back as an
error carrying the offset of the offending character.

fields.name: rsqlFields
fields.description:
Every field a smart-playlist filter may mention, so a form can offer a
picker rather than expecting the vocabulary to be memorised.

fields.name: radioStations
fields.description:
The user's own stations — the ones added by hand here, on atradio.fm, or
on another device. A subset of the bookmarks, told apart by their source.

fields.name: checkRadioStream
fields.description: Check a stream url before the "add station" form saves it.

types.name: RsqlField
types.description:
One filterable field, so a UI can offer a picker instead of making the user
remember the vocabulary.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name to write in a filter.

fields.name: label
fields.description: A human label.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: `text`, `integer`, `boolean` or `timestamp` — what values it accepts.

types.name: SmartPlaylistInput
types.description: The three things a smart playlist is: a filter, an order, and a cap.

inputFields.name: filter
inputFields.description:
RSQL over the track fields, e.g. `genre==rock;year>2000`. Empty matches
the whole library.

inputFields.name: sortBy
inputFields.description: A track field to order by, or `random`.

inputFields.name: limit
inputFields.description: Maximum number of tracks. Absent or 0 is unlimited.

types.name: SmartPlaylistPreview
types.description:
What a filter would produce, without saving anything — the "142 tracks
match" line under the filter box, plus the first few by name.

fields.name: count
fields.description: How many tracks the filter matches.

fields.name: tracks
fields.description: The first handful, so the form can show what it caught.

types.name: StreamCheck
types.description:
The verdict on a stream url, so the form can say what is wrong before the
station is saved — and fill itself in from the station's own ICY headers
when it is right.

types.name: String
types.description:
The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8
character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to
represent free-form human-readable text.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type
validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution
behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally
including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing
additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description:
A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a
__DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description:
One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a
placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned
in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description:
Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which
has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description:
Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an
InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and
optionally a default value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description:
A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes
all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry
points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
description of __Schema for newer graphiql introspection schema
requirements

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description:
If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will
be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description:
If this server support subscription, the type that subscription
operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds
of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about
that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and
description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface
types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface,
provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose
other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid
fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are
valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: A reason for why it is deprecated, formatted using Markdown syntax

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: oneOf
directives.description: Indicates that an Input Object is a OneOf Input Object (and thus requires exactly one of its field be provided)

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Provides a scalar specification URL for specifying the behavior of custom scalar types.

args.name: url
args.description: URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.
